title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context, from the surrounding pages: in the July 1986 notes on 'ateliers', Grothendieck works with a 'magasin' M. This is a set carrying three structures: a preorder ⊴; a stronger relation °≪ (to be read as 'X lies well inside Y', non-tangential inclusion); and a symmetric relation |o| (to be read as 'X and Y are disjoint / separated'). These are subject to axioms Mag 1–4. An 'atelier' attached to M is a family F ⊂ 𝔓(M), apparently an analogue of the lattice of opens.

Previous page (Digression 1): the direct sum M = ∐ M_i. Its ⊴ and °≪ are the disjoint sums of the given relations. Elements in different summands are declared |o|, and inside one summand |o| is the original relation. The sum of ateliers is F = {A ⊂ M : A∩M_i ∈ F_i for all i}, so F ≅ ∏ F_i as ordered sets.

This page comments on that construction in two ways.

(1) A categorical caveat. Grothendieck warns that this 'sum' is not (or not yet known to be) a coproduct for the notion of morphism of magasins introduced so far. He adds parenthetically that it would be nice if it were. The reason is the geometric interpretation, with gluing of 'infinitesimal arrows': there the sum of magasins really does correspond to a disjoint sum of spaces. He also remarks that it is at the same time a product, as the gluing principle suggests. This matches F ≅ ∏ F_i, just as Open(∐X_i) = ∏ Open(X_i).

(2) A converse decomposition. Starting from any magasin M, define its connected components M_i as the classes of the equivalence relation generated by °≪. One wants M to be the sum of its components. That requires an extra axiom, which he says will be much strengthened later:
- Magconnexe: if X, Y ∈ M belong to distinct connected components, then X |o| Y.

Under this axiom, M ≅ ∐ M_i. This is the abstract analogue of: a space is the disjoint union of its components when distinct components are separated. A marginal note seems to refer to the condition involving |o|.
errors: Gap: the components are defined using °≪ only. For M to be the sum of its components one also needs ⊴ to relate no elements of different components. This is presumably derivable from Mag 1–4 (e.g. via an approximation axiom linking ⊴ and °≪), but it is not checked on the page.
The claim that the sum is not a categorical coproduct is stated without proof, and it depends on a notion of morphism not visible here. It is a caution rather than a result.

ideas.what: Direct sum of magasins/ateliers; the atelier of a sum is the product of the ateliers (like Open(∐X_i) = ∏ Open(X_i))
ideas.modern_name: coproduct of spaces / product of frames; sums of contact or proximity algebras

ideas.what: Remark that the naive sum need not be a categorical coproduct for the current notion of morphism, while geometrically it should be
ideas.modern_name: choice of morphisms so that disjoint unions are coproducts

ideas.what: Connected components via the equivalence relation generated by the 'well-inside' relation, plus the axiom Magconnexe (distinct components are disjoint, |o|) giving a decomposition into a sum
ideas.modern_name: connectedness in contact algebras / mereotopology (connected regions, decomposition into components)
ideas.usually_credited_to: mereotopology: Clarke 1981; Randell–Cui–Cohn 1992 (RCC); Vakarelov, Düntsch et al. (contact algebras, 2000s); de Vries 1962 (compingent algebras)

missed.claim: The magasin primitives closely parallel the basic relations of region-based theories of space (mereotopology, RCC, contact and proximity algebras). ⊴ plays the part-of relation, °≪ the non-tangential proper part ('well inside'), and |o| the 'disconnected/disjoint' relation (DC/DR). Here Grothendieck treats sums and connected components of such structures, with an explicit gluing axiom. To my knowledge, the 1986 'ateliers/magasins' notes have not been related to this literature.
missed.quote: définir ses composantes connexes M_i, comme les composantes connexes pour la relation ≪ : On trouve une décomposition en somme, à condition de supposer [l'axiome suivant] ... Magconnexe Si X, Y ∈ M appartiennent à des composantes connexes distinctes de M, on a X |o| Y.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Grothendieck's 1986 'pointless' topology project would then be an independent foundation of region-based topology, contemporaneous with Clarke and predating RCC. A comparison could show whether his axioms (with ateliers as 'open families') give a duality with spaces similar to de Vries duality.

missed.claim: He asks whether the sum could be made a genuine categorical coproduct, by adjusting the notion of morphism of magasins in line with the 'gluing of infinitesimal arrows' interpretation. He also notes that it is simultaneously a product. This is left open here.
missed.quote: ce ne serait pas mal ... la somme de magasins correspond bien à une somme d'espaces. C'est aussi un produit, comme pourrait le suggérer le principe de recollement des flèches
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is minor, but it signals the intended categorical framework (morphisms as gluings of infinitesimal arrows), which is not visible in any published text.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on the page is routine: sums and connected components. The interest is that it documents an unpublished 1986 axiomatic, region-based topology whose primitives resemble mereotopology and contact algebras. That link appears unexplored, but the page itself contains no deep result.
transcription_corrections: Line 3 likely reads '(pour la notion de morphismes de magasins introduite jusqu'à présent)' rather than 'recollements'.
'(ce qui serait pas mal?)' is probably '(ce ne serait pas mal?)', and 'ou l'interprétation' is probably 'vu l'interprétation'.
'Cet aussi un produit' should read 'C'est aussi un produit'.
'à condition de supposer l'existence ...' is probably 'à condition de supposer l'axiome suivant (qui sera beaucoup renforcé par la suite)'.
'Si X, Y ⊂ M réunions de composantes connexes distinctes' should read 'Si X, Y ∈ M appartiennent à des composantes connexes distinctes de M, on a X|o|Y'.
'Magconnexe' (axiom label) is underlined; 'on peut songer à définir'.
